3	/// The agent's silence tool: the read half of Remove Silences.
4	///
5	/// `detect_silence` is an APP-STATE tool, not an op — it changes nothing and
6	/// registers no undo step. It exists because the detection is Swift's (the
7	/// waveform peaks the package caches are not in the model, and the core does
8	/// no sample work at all — spec §7), so an agent that could only call
9	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` would have to invent the ranges from nothing. The
10	/// pair is deliberate and mirrors the sheet exactly: `detect_silence` is what
11	/// `SilenceSheetController` shows in its live readout, and
12	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` is what its Remove button sends.
13	///
14	/// It stays on the MAIN thread, and so out of `AgentServer.offMainTools`,
15	/// because that set's criterion is "waits for something the main thread has
16	/// to deliver or must not be doing", not "touches the disk":
17	/// `consolidate_media` copies whole media libraries on main and says why, and
18	/// `import_captions` parses a file on main for the same reason. Reading a few
19	/// hundred KB of `cache/peaks/<id>.bin` and making one arithmetic pass over
20	/// it waits on nothing and has no completion to deliver, and being off main
21	/// would cost an `onMain` hop for every document touch — which is where the
22	/// real bugs in this file's neighbours have been.
23	extension AgentServer {
24	
25	    /// The longest a duration argument may be, `snappedTick`'s own ±9.0e15:
26	    /// past it `refine`'s `run.start + padding` overflows. Finding 1 above.
27	    /// Not private: `AgentCatalog+Audio` PUBLISHES it as both durations'
28	    /// `maximum`, so the bound a caller reads and the bound the handler
29	    /// enforces are one number (the second sceptic pass, road map 4 §8).
30	    static let durationCeiling = 9_000_000_000_000_000
31	
32	    /// `detect_silence` — Clip ▸ Remove Silences…
33	    /// (`SilenceSheetController`, whose four controls are these four
34	    /// arguments and whose live "N cuts · removes M:SS" line is this
35	    /// result). Nothing is edited: feed `ranges` to `ripple_delete_ranges`
36	    /// to make the cut, which is what that sheet's button does. The
37	    /// `protected_nests` note is the tool's spelling of the sheet's nest note.
38	    ///
39	    /// Quiet is measured IN THE MIX — the peak bucket times the plan's audio
40	    /// envelope at that tick — so a clip turned down, faded, ducked, muted or
41	    /// silenced by another track's solo is quiet here exactly as it is in the
42	    /// speakers. A tick no clip in scope covers is not a candidate at all: a
43	    /// hole in the timeline is not dead air to be removed.
44	    func detectSilence(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
45	        let document = try target(a)
46	        let clips = try optionalClipsArg(a, "clips", document)
47	        // `clips` is the sheet's scope popup, spelled as the thing an agent
48	        // actually has: ids. Naming any runs the popup's "Selected clips"
49	        // over exactly those — `read` takes a selection override for this
50	        // very reason — and omitting the key takes the sheet's own opening
51	        // rule, which is the document's selection when it holds anything
52	        // with sound and everything audible otherwise. The result reports
53	        // which of the two answered, because "nothing was found" and
54	        // "nothing was looked at" are different answers and no caller can
55	        // tell them apart from an empty list.
56	        guard let input = SilenceDetector.read(from: document, selection: clips.map { Set($0) })
57	        else {
58	            throw ToolError(
59	                message: "The project's audio plan could not be read, so there is nothing to "
60	                    + "measure silence against.")
61	        }
62	        let (settings, modeNote) = try silenceSettings(
63	            a, scope: clips == nil ? input.defaultScope : .selected,
64	            voiceAvailable: input.voiceAvailable)
65	        let outcome = SilenceDetector.detect(input, settings: settings)
66	
67	        var result: [String: Any] = [
68	            "ok": true,
69	            "ranges": outcome.spans.map { [$0.start, $0.end] },
70	            "count": outcome.spans.count,
71	            "removes": outcome.removed,
72	            "scope": outcome.scope.rawValue,
73	            "clips": outcome.clips.map { Int($0) },
74	            "threshold_db": settings.thresholdDB,
75	            "min_length": settings.minLength,
76	            "padding": settings.padding,
77	            "mode": outcome.mode.rawValue,
78	            "voice_confidence": settings.voiceConfidence,
79	            "judged_by_level": outcome.judgedByLevel.map { Int($0) },
80	            // The same answers by CLIP (#107): two clips of one file can be
81	            // judged, and proposed, differently.
82	            "judged_by_level_clips": outcome.judgedByLevelClips.map { Int($0) },
83	        ]
84	        if !outcome.proposedByMixClips.isEmpty {
85	            result["proposed_by_mix_clips"] = outcome.proposedByMixClips.map { Int($0) }
86	        }
87	        var notes: [String] = []
88	        if let modeNote { notes.append(modeNote) }
89	        // Two things worth a sentence rather than a silent zero, because both
90	        // read as "there is no dead air here" and neither is that.
91	        if outcome.clips.isEmpty {
92	            notes.append(
93	                settings.scope == .selected
94	                ? "None of those clips plays any sound, so nothing was analysed."
95	                : "Nothing in this timeline is audible, so nothing was analysed.")
96	        }
97	        // Both waiters fold into ONE key, `pending_peaks` — the union of what
98	        // the level test and the voice test are each still waiting on — so a
99	        // caller that only ever read that key still knows to call again.
100	        let pendingPeaks = Set(outcome.pendingMedia)
101	        let pendingUnion = outcome.mode == .voice
102	            ? pendingPeaks.union(outcome.voicePending) : pendingPeaks
103	        if !pendingUnion.isEmpty {
104	            result["pending_peaks"] = pendingUnion.sorted().map { Int($0) }
105	            // "Nothing inside them is proposed for removal" is a PROMISE about
106	            // the ranges in this same reply, so it is made only about the
107	            // media it holds for. A media with no peaks is never quiet in
108	            // LEVEL mode, so there it holds for every waiter; in VOICE mode a
109	            // media whose waveform is missing but whose speech has landed is
110	            // judged by the model and spans inside it ARE proposed — and the
111	            // sentence used to deny exactly the ranges it was printed beside
112	            // (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R3·1).
113	            let waiter = outcome.mode == .voice ? Set(outcome.voicePending) : pendingPeaks
114	            // And the promise is made about what this ANSWER shows, not about
115	            // the mode: the gain FLOOR is asked before either cache
116	            // (`SilenceDetector.isQuiet`), so a clip the mix has turned down,
117	            // faded, ducked or muted is quiet with nothing on disk at all and
118	            // its spans are right here (the reader review, road map 4 §8,
119	            // finding 2). Whatever the answer proposes inside is dropped from
120	            // the promise, and the clips it is proposed inside are named in
121	            // their own clause (#107).
122	            let proposedInside = waiter.intersection(outcome.proposedMedia)
123	            let blocked = waiter.subtracting(proposedInside)
124	            let waveformOnly = pendingUnion.subtracting(waiter)
125	            var waiting =
126	                "Analysis is still running for \(pendingUnion.count) media file(s); call "
127	                + "again in a moment."
128	            if !blocked.isEmpty {
129	                waiting += blocked.count == pendingUnion.count
130	                    ? " Nothing inside them is proposed for removal."
131	                    : " Nothing inside \(blocked.count) of them is proposed for removal."
132	            }
133	            let mixInside = Self.clipIDs(outcome.mixAnswers(inside: waiter))
134	            if mixInside.count == 1 {
135	                waiting +=
136	                    " Clip \(mixInside[0]) holds spans that ARE proposed here: the mix turns "
137	                    + "it down far enough to be quiet before either cache is asked."
138	            } else if mixInside.count > 1 {
139	                waiting +=
140	                    " Clips \(Self.listed(mixInside)) hold spans that ARE proposed here: the "
141	                    + "mix turns them down far enough to be quiet before either cache is asked."
142	            }
143	            if !waveformOnly.isEmpty {
144	                // The mirror image of the promise above, and it needs the
145	                // same intersection (the reader review's second sceptic pass,
146	                // road map 4 §8). "Spans inside them ARE proposed here" is a
147	                // claim about ranges in this very reply, so a waveform waiter
148	                // the answer proposes NOTHING inside — every clip of it holds
149	                // no voice, so the missing waveform blocks the lot — must not
150	                // be told it has them.
151	                let proposedHere = waveformOnly.intersection(outcome.proposedMedia)
152	                let silentHere = waveformOnly.subtracting(proposedHere)
153	                let ending: String
154	                if silentHere.isEmpty {
155	                    ending = ", so spans inside them ARE proposed here."
156	                } else if proposedHere.isEmpty {
157	                    ending = ", and nothing inside them is proposed here."
158	                } else {
159	                    ending =
160	                        ", so spans inside \(proposedHere.count) of them ARE proposed here "
161	                        + "and nothing inside the other \(silentHere.count) is."
162	                }
163	                waiting +=
164	                    " For \(Self.subject(waveformOnly.count, of: pendingUnion.count)) it is the "
165	                    + "WAVEFORM that has not landed, which in voice mode decides only a clip "
166	                    + "holding no voice" + ending
167	                // And where those spans are the FLOOR's rather than the
168	                // model's, name the clip (#107): a clip that holds no voice
169	                // is proposed without its waveform only because the mix
170	                // already turned it down, and another clip of the same file
171	                // the mix left alone is not. No `voicePending` arm is needed
172	                // here — a voice waiter is in `waiter` above and never in
173	                // `waveformOnly`.
174	                let mixOnly = Self.clipIDs(outcome.mixAnswers(inside: waveformOnly))
175	                if mixOnly.count == 1 {
176	                    waiting +=
177	                        " Clip \(mixOnly[0]) is proposed only where the mix already turns it "
178	                        + "down far enough to be quiet."
179	                } else if mixOnly.count > 1 {
180	                    waiting +=
181	                        " Clips \(Self.listed(mixOnly)) are proposed only where the mix "
182	                        + "already turns them down far enough to be quiet."
183	                }
184	            }
185	            notes.append(waiting)
186	        }
187	        if !outcome.voicePending.isEmpty {
188	            result["voice_pending"] = outcome.voicePending.map { Int($0) }
189	        }
190	        let byLevel = outcome.judgedByLevelClips
191	        if byLevel.count == 1 {
192	            notes.append("Clip \(byLevel[0]) holds no voice and was judged by level.")
193	        } else if byLevel.count > 1 {
194	            notes.append(
195	                "Clips \(Self.listed(byLevel)) hold no voice and were judged by level.")
196	        }
197	        // The sheet's nest note, spelled for an agent (#352): a candidate
198	        // held back at a nest's wall, dropped without a word, reads as "there
199	        // is no dead air here". A listed nest clip is one a quiet run of the
200	        // SCOPED voices crossed (`SilenceDetector+Walls.swift`'s
201	        // `excludingNests`); the nest's own sound is not tested, so it MAY
202	        // hold dead air, and the reader is told to look, not that it does.
203	        // Last, as the sheet puts its nest note last.
204	        if !outcome.protectedNests.isEmpty {
205	            let ids = outcome.protectedNests
206	            result["protected_nests"] = ids.map { Int($0) }

208	                ids.count == 1

211	            let reach =

216	                    + "detect_silence again."

218	                lead + ": a nest plays from its first frame, so cutting into one would "
219	                    + "strand the rest of it. " + reach)
220	        }
221	        if !notes.isEmpty { result["note"] = notes.joined(separator: " ") }
222	        result["project"] = summary(document)
223	        return try jsonResult(result)

226	    /// "that file" / "them" / "2 of them", so a clause about SOME of the
227	    /// waiters never says "the rest" of a sentence that was not printed
228	    /// (the reader review, road map 4 §8, finding 4).
229	    private static func subject(_ count: Int, of total: Int) -> String {
230	        count == total ? (count == 1 ? "that file" : "them") : "\(count) of them"
231	    }

233	    /// The distinct clip ids of some voices' answers, ascending — the tool
234	    /// names a clip by id, as `Transcriber+Jobs` tags one (#107).
235	    private static func clipIDs(_ answers: [SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer]) -> [UInt32] {
236	        Set(answers.map { $0.clip }).sorted()
237	    }
238	
239	    /// "3, 7, 9".
240	    private static func listed(_ ids: [UInt32]) -> String {
241	        ids.map { String($0) }.joined(separator: ", ")
242	    }

244	    /// The three numbers, read in the sheet's own units and refused by name.
245	    ///
246	    /// The sheet clamps its controls to `Settings`' published ranges because
247	    /// a slider must land somewhere; a tool does not, and clamping an
248	    /// argument silently would report a detection the caller did not ask
249	    /// for. What is refused here is what is not a level or not a length at
250	    /// all — everything else is passed through and named back in the result,
251	    /// so a caller reading `threshold_db` sees what actually ran.
252	    private func silenceSettings(
253	        _ a: [String: Any], scope: SilenceDetector.Scope, voiceAvailable: Bool
254	    ) throws -> (SilenceDetector.Settings, String?) {
255	        var settings = SilenceDetector.Settings(scope: scope)
256	        var note: String?
257	        if let modeString = try stringArg(a, "mode") {
258	            guard let mode = SilenceDetector.Mode(rawValue: modeString) else {
259	                throw ToolError(
260	                    message: "mode must be \"voice\" or \"level\".")
261	            }
262	            if mode == .voice, !voiceAvailable {
263	                throw ToolError(
264	                    message: "The voice model could not be used; call with mode: \"level\".")
265	            }
266	            settings.mode = mode
267	        } else if !voiceAvailable {
268	            settings.mode = .level
269	            note = "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level."
270	        }
271	        if let voiceConfidence = try doubleArg(a, "voice_confidence") {
272	            guard settings.mode == .voice else {
273	                throw ToolError(
274	                    message: "voice_confidence only applies in mode: \"voice\".")
275	            }
276	            guard voiceConfidence.isFinite,
277	                SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.contains(voiceConfidence)
278	            else {
279	                throw ToolError(
280	                    message: "voice_confidence must be a number in "
281	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.lowerBound)…"
282	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.upperBound).")
283	            }
284	            settings.voiceConfidence = voiceConfidence
285	        }
286	        if let thresholdDB = try doubleArg(a, "threshold_db") {
287	            // Above full scale every bucket of every recording counts as
288	            // quiet and the whole timeline comes back as one candidate.
289	            // Peaks are unclamped and a hot source really does read over
290	            // 1.0, so this is a caller's mistake — a level in gain, or a
291	            // sign forgotten — rather than an impossible number.
292	            guard thresholdDB.isFinite, thresholdDB <= 0 else {
293	                throw ToolError(
294	                    message: "threshold_db must be a level at or below 0 dBFS (full scale); "
295	                        + "the default is \(SilenceDetector.Settings.defaultThresholdDB).")
296	            }
297	            settings.thresholdDB = thresholdDB
298	        }
299	        // Both lengths are DURATIONS, and a duration is not a position: they
300	        // are read as given, by the whole-number reader, and are NOT snapped
301	        // to the frame grid. The sheet's own two fields are not snapped
302	        // either (`SilenceSheetController.silenceSettings`'
303	        // `ReelTime.ticks(seconds:)`) and this tool exists to mirror it; the
304	        // frame rule stays where it belongs, on the span BOUNDS `refine`
305	        // produces, so no sub-frame time reaches an op from here. Going
306	        // through `optionalTimeArg` cost that mirror at the DEFAULT rate:
307	        // at 30 fps it ran `padding: 30000` — the sheet's own 0.05 s — as
308	        // 40000, ran `min_length: 45000` as 40000, and dropped
309	        // `padding: 9999` to 0, cutting the material the caller asked to
310	        // keep (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R1·1).
311	        //
312	        // What `optionalTimeArg` DID carry and a duration still needs is its
313	        // CEILING: `refine` adds the padding to a run's start, and a padding
314	        // at `Int64.max` overflowed and killed the app rather than answering
315	        // (the reader review, road map 4 §8, finding 1). The bound is
316	        // `snappedTick`'s own ±9.0e15, refused in a sentence naming the
317	        // argument. The sheet's two fields cannot reach it — they clamp to
318	        // `minLengthRange` and `paddingRange` — so the guard belongs here,
319	        // on the one caller that is not a slider.
320	        if let minLength = try intArg(a, "min_length") {
321	            guard minLength >= 0, minLength <= Self.durationCeiling else {
322	                throw ToolError(
323	                    message: "min_length must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
324	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
325	            }
326	            settings.minLength = Ticks(minLength)
327	        }
328	        if let padding = try intArg(a, "padding") {
329	            guard padding >= 0, padding <= Self.durationCeiling else {
330	                throw ToolError(
331	                    message: "padding must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
332	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
333	            }
334	            settings.padding = Ticks(padding)
335	        }
336	        return (settings, note)
337	    }
338	}

3	/// Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words… — road map "cut-by-transcript" CT-3 (spec §11
4	/// TR-4, TR-7, TR-10): `detect_fillers`' answer as a count, the same spans
5	/// washed onto the timeline behind the sheet, and one `ripple_delete_ranges`
6	/// op when Remove is pressed.
7	///
8	/// **`SilenceSheetController`'s shape, without its controls.** TR-9 has no
9	/// threshold, padding or length to tune, so there is nothing to change and
10	/// `refresh()` runs only when the input does: at open, and after a
11	/// Transcribe run lands a filler transcript. The input is read once by the
12	/// command, as Remove Silences' is, because the document cannot change under
13	/// an open sheet — every editor action validates false while one is attached.
14	///
15	/// **The media with no filler transcript** (TR-7: the fillers come only from
16	/// an AssemblyAI transcript that asked for them) get a section of their own:
17	/// the cloud-only note, where the audio goes (R6-2), and one row per media
18	/// with its estimate and a Transcribe button
19	/// (`FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift`). A run is one media's paid
20	/// upload, so Remove is disabled while it goes: Return cannot cut, and Cancel
21	/// is the only default-key path left, which stops the run.
22	final class FillerSheetController: NSViewController {

24	    /// close even with a dialog mid-air.

27	    /// sheet sets it and the sheet clears it.

34	    let cacheDirectory: URL?

36	    /// `TranscribeSheetController`'s injection points, for the probe.
37	    let store: any SecretStore
38	    let defaults: UserDefaults

40	
41	    /// What the sheet currently describes. Remove sends exactly these spans,

43	    private(set) var outcome: FillerDetector.Outcome
44	    /// The media a Transcribe run is going for, or nil when none is.

60	    /// The TR-7 section's second line: R6-2's where, which region, and the

181	    /// Re-detect and republish everything that follows from it: the readout,

197	        let cuts = outcome.spans.count == 1 ? "1 cut" : "\(outcome.spans.count) cuts"
198	        return cuts + " · removes " + ReelTime.format(outcome.removed, fps: input.fps, frames: true)

296	        else {

301	        // The wash is read while the sheet is up, and a running playhead
302	        // repaints over it several times a second.

306	            cacheDirectory: document.cacheDirectory)

321	        return ModelKeys.mark(item, missing: missing, enabled: playable && missing == nil)

326	/// transcript (spec §11 CJ-12) — the menu validator's question, asked every
327	/// time a menu opens. One entry, kept while the edited project's handle, the
328	/// selection, the cache directory and `<cache>/transcripts/`'s modification
329	/// date are the ones it was answered for: the transcript cache posts nothing,
330	/// and a transcript written or removed renames an entry in that folder.
331	enum FillerTranscriptPresence {
332	    private struct Key {
333	        let project: ReelProject
334	        let selection: Set<UInt32>
335	        let cache: URL?
336	        let stamp: Date?
337	    }
338	
339	    private static var memo: (key: Key, answer: Bool)?
340	
341	    static func any(in document: ProjectDocument) -> Bool {
342	        let cache = document.cacheDirectory
343	        let folder = cache?.appendingPathComponent(MediaImporter.transcriptsKind, isDirectory: true)
344	        let stamp = folder.flatMap {
345	            try? $0.resourceValues(forKeys: [.contentModificationDateKey]).contentModificationDate
346	        }
347	        let key = Key(
348	            project: document.editedProject, selection: document.selection, cache: cache,
349	            stamp: stamp)
350	        if let memo, memo.key.project === key.project, memo.key.selection == key.selection,
351	            memo.key.cache == key.cache, memo.key.stamp == key.stamp
352	        {
353	            return memo.answer
354	        }
355	        let answer = !FillerDetector.read(from: document, clips: nil).clips.isEmpty
356	        memo = (key, answer)
357	        return answer
358	    }
359	}

3	/// Remove Filler Words' detector (road map "cut-by-transcript" CT-2, spec §11
4	/// TR-4, TR-7, TR-9): a clip's cached cloud filler words as project ranges
5	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` cuts, every edge on the Silero 32 ms grid and then
6	/// on the frame grid.
7	///
8	/// `SilenceDetector`'s shape: `read(from:clips:)` is the one seam that touches
9	/// a document — its snapshot, its selection, its media URLs and the transcript
10	/// cache, read ONCE — and everything after it (`runs`, `gridded`, `placed`,
11	/// `detect`) is arithmetic over values. The words are a Swift cache like the
12	/// peaks (spec §7), so nothing here crosses the FFI.
13	///
14	/// **Only a transcript that asked for fillers is read** (TR-7): the scope's
15	/// files come through `fillersFile`, whose marker must serve `.fillers`
16	/// (TR-2's one rule, `TranscriptStamp.serves`). A media without one is named
17	/// in `needsTranscript` and gives no candidate. The NEIGHBOURS' words — which
18	/// protect a span from a cut — are taken from any transcript that serves
19	/// `.captions`, because a word is a word whichever request heard it.
20	///
21	/// **TR-9, the edges.** A run of consecutive fillers is widened OUTWARD to the
22	/// grid so the whole filler goes, but never past the words beside it; each
23	/// edge then maps to project time through `MediaTranscript.project` (R6-10's
24	/// door) and snaps INWARD to the frame grid, as Remove Silences snaps. A
25	/// candidate that would cut into another clip's word, a nest clip or a
26	/// transition is dropped whole, never trimmed, so every kept edge is a grid
27	/// edge.
28	enum FillerDetector {
29	
30	    /// The Silero VAD's chunk in source ticks (512 samples at 16 kHz), from
31	    /// absolute source time 0 — the speech cache's own index.
32	    static var grid: Ticks { MediaSpeech.chunkTicks }
33	
34	    /// Which clips were read: the ones named or selected, or every clip.
35	    enum Scope: String { case selected, all }
36	
37	    /// One clip's job and the transcript file of its media.
38	    struct ClipWords {
39	        let job: Transcriber.Job
40	        let file: MediaTranscript.File
41	    }
42	
43	    /// Everything a detection reads, taken off the document once.
44	    struct Input {
45	        let fps: Fps
46	        let scope: Scope
47	        /// The scope's clips whose media has a transcript that asked for fillers.
48	        let clips: [ClipWords]
49	        /// Media ids in scope with no such transcript, sorted and distinct.
50	        let needsTranscript: [UInt32]
51	        /// The named clips `Transcriber.jobs` refused, each with its reason.
52	        let skipped: [CaptionLayout.Problem]
53	        /// In-scope clip ids on locked tracks, sorted: the ripple neither cuts
54	        /// nor moves a locked track, so their fillers are not read.
55	        let locked: [UInt32]
56	        /// Every top-level clip on an unlocked track whose media's transcript
57	        /// serves `.captions`, in scope or not: the ripple cuts every
58	        /// unlocked track, so their words protect a span.
59	        let neighbours: [ClipWords]
60	        let nests: [SilenceDetector.NestExtent]
61	        let walls: [SilenceDetector.Span]
62	    }
63	
64	    /// One run of consecutive fillers in a clip's word order, in source ticks.
65	    struct Run: Equatable {
66	        let words: [String]
67	        let source: SilenceDetector.Span
68	        /// The latest end of a non-filler word before the run, or the clip's `in`.
69	        let previousEnd: Ticks
70	        /// The earliest start of a non-filler word after it, or the window's end.
71	        let nextStart: Ticks
72	    }
73	
74	    /// A run that became a cut: its source span on the grid and its project span.
75	    struct Candidate: Equatable {
76	        let clip: UInt32
77	        let words: [String]
78	        let source: SilenceDetector.Span
79	        let span: SilenceDetector.Span
80	    }
81	
82	    enum DropReason: Equatable {
83	        case tooShort
84	        case overlapsWord(clip: UInt32, text: String)
85	        case nest(clip: UInt32)
86	        case transition
87	    }
88	
89	    struct Dropped: Equatable {
90	        let clip: UInt32
91	        let words: [String]
92	        let reason: DropReason
93	    }
94	
95	    struct Outcome {
96	        /// The kept candidates merged where they overlap or touch.
97	        let spans: [SilenceDetector.Span]
98	        let candidates: [Candidate]
99	        let dropped: [Dropped]
100	        let scope: Scope
101	        /// The clips whose words were read, sorted.
102	        let clips: [UInt32]
103	        let needsTranscript: [UInt32]
104	        let skipped: [CaptionLayout.Problem]
105	        let locked: [UInt32]
106	
107	        var removed: Ticks { spans.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.length } }
108	    }
109	
110	    // MARK: - The read
111	
112	    /// The document's snapshot, scope and transcript cache, read once.
113	    ///
114	    /// Named clips are the scope (`.selected`); with none named, the
115	    /// selection when `Transcriber.jobs` accepts any of it, else every clip.
116	    /// The EDITED project, as `SilenceDetector.read` takes it: with a nest
117	    /// open the ranges are the nest's, in the nest's own time.
118	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips named: [UInt32]?) -> Input {
119	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
120	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
121	        let maps = document.editedProject.sourceMap
122	        let scope: Scope
123	        let chosen: [ClipSnapshot]
124	        if let named {
125	            let ids = Set(named)
126	            chosen = snapshot.clips.filter { ids.contains($0.id) }
127	            scope = .selected
128	        } else {
129	            let selected = snapshot.clips.filter { document.selection.contains($0.id) }
130	            if !Transcriber.jobs(for: selected, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps).jobs.isEmpty {
131	                chosen = selected
132	                scope = .selected
133	            } else {
134	                chosen = snapshot.clips
135	                scope = .all
136	            }
137	        }
138	        let (kept, locked) = onUnlockedTracks(chosen, in: snapshot)
139	        let (jobs, problems) = Transcriber.jobs(for: kept, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps)
140	        let cacheDirectory = document.cacheDirectory
141	
142	        var clips: [ClipWords] = []
143	        var needs: Set<UInt32> = []
144	        var scopeFiles: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File?] = [:]
145	        for job in jobs {
146	            if scopeFiles[job.media] == nil {
147	                scopeFiles[job.media] = .some(
148	                    cacheDirectory.flatMap { cache in
149	                        snapshot.media(job.media).flatMap {
150	                            fillersFile(for: $0, url: job.source, in: cache)
151	                        }
152	                    })
153	            }
154	            if let file = scopeFiles[job.media] ?? nil {
155	                clips.append(ClipWords(job: job, file: file))
156	            } else {
157	                needs.insert(job.media)
158	            }
159	        }
160	
161	        var neighbours: [ClipWords] = []
162	        if let cacheDirectory {
163	            let unlocked = onUnlockedTracks(snapshot.clips, in: snapshot).kept
164	            var files: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File?] = [:]
165	            let found = Transcriber.jobs(for: unlocked, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps)
166	            for job in found.jobs {
167	                if files[job.media] == nil {
168	                    files[job.media] = .some(
169	                        snapshot.media(job.media).flatMap {
170	                            transcriptFile(
171	                                for: $0, url: job.source, in: cacheDirectory, use: .captions)
172	                        })
173	                }
174	                if let file = files[job.media] ?? nil {
175	                    neighbours.append(ClipWords(job: job, file: file))
176	                }
177	            }
178	        }
179	        return Input(
180	            fps: snapshot.canvas.fps, scope: scope, clips: clips, needsTranscript: needs.sorted(),
181	            skipped: named == nil ? [] : problems, locked: locked, neighbours: neighbours,
182	            nests: SilenceDetector.nestExtents(in: snapshot),
183	            walls: SilenceDetector.overlapWalls(snapshot))
184	    }

186	    /// The scope's door: a media's transcript only when its marker serves
187	    /// filler removal (TR-7, TR-2).
188	    static func fillersFile(
189	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, in cacheDir: URL
190	    ) -> MediaTranscript.File? {
191	        transcriptFile(for: media, url: url, in: cacheDir, use: .fillers)
192	    }
193	
194	    /// A media's cached transcript when the file as it is NOW stamps the
195	    /// marker's source, the file reads, and the marker serves `use` for the
196	    /// request the file records; else nil.
197	    static func transcriptFile(
198	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, in cacheDir: URL, use: TranscriptUse
199	    ) -> MediaTranscript.File? {
200	        guard let stamp = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: media, url: url),
201	            let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: media.id, in: cacheDir),
202	            let marker = MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: media.id, in: cacheDir),
203	            marker.serves(TranscriptStamp(source: stamp, options: file.header.requested), for: use)
204	        else { return nil }

206	    }

208	    /// The clips not on a locked track, and the ids of those that are,
209	    /// sorted. A track the snapshot cannot find counts as unlocked, as the
210	    /// nest walls read it.
211	    static func onUnlockedTracks(
212	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
213	    ) -> (kept: [ClipSnapshot], locked: [UInt32]) {
214	        var kept: [ClipSnapshot] = []
215	        var locked: [UInt32] = []
216	        for clip in clips {
217	            if snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked == true {
218	                locked.append(clip.id)
219	            } else {
220	                kept.append(clip)
221	            }
222	        }
223	        return (kept, locked.sorted())
224	    }

226	    // MARK: - The arithmetic
227	
228	    /// One word of a clip's window, in source ticks.
229	    private struct Timed {
230	        let text: String
231	        let start: Ticks
232	        let end: Ticks
233	        let filler: Bool
234	    }
235	
236	    /// The clip's words in source ticks: those whose start is in its window
237	    /// (R6-10), sorted by start then end.
238	    private static func timed(_ file: MediaTranscript.File, in job: Transcriber.Job) -> [Timed] {
239	        let windowEnd = job.sourceIn + job.sourceLength
240	        var out: [Timed] = []
241	        for word in file.words {
242	            let start = MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: word.start)
243	            guard start >= job.sourceIn, start < windowEnd else { continue }
244	            out.append(
245	                Timed(
246	                    text: word.text, start: start,
247	                    end: MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: max(word.start, word.end)),
248	                    filler: FillerWords.isFiller(word.text)))
249	        }
250	        return out.sorted { ($0.start, $0.end) < ($1.start, $1.end) }
251	    }
252	
253	    /// Every maximal run of consecutive fillers in the clip's word order,
254	    /// with the non-filler words that bound it (TR-9).
255	    static func runs(of file: MediaTranscript.File, in job: Transcriber.Job) -> [Run] {
256	        let words = timed(file, in: job)
257	        let windowEnd = job.sourceIn + job.sourceLength
258	        // The latest non-filler end before each index, and the earliest
259	        // non-filler start after it.
260	        var before = [Ticks](repeating: job.sourceIn, count: words.count + 1)
261	        for (index, word) in words.enumerated() {
262	            before[index + 1] = word.filler ? before[index] : max(before[index], word.end)
263	        }
264	        var after = [Ticks](repeating: windowEnd, count: words.count + 1)
265	        for index in stride(from: words.count - 1, through: 0, by: -1) {
266	            let word = words[index]
267	            after[index] = word.filler ? after[index + 1] : min(after[index + 1], word.start)
268	        }
269	        var runs: [Run] = []
270	        var open: [Int] = []
271	        func close() {
272	            guard let first = open.first, let last = open.last else { return }
273	            runs.append(
274	                Run(
275	                    words: open.map { words[$0].text },
276	                    source: SilenceDetector.Span(
277	                        start: words[first].start, end: open.map { words[$0].end }.max() ?? 0),
278	                    previousEnd: before[first], nextStart: after[last + 1]))
279	            open = []
280	        }
281	        for (index, word) in words.enumerated() {
282	            guard word.filler else {
283	                close()
284	                continue
285	            }
286	            open.append(index)
287	        }
288	        close()
289	        return runs
290	    }
291	
292	    private static func down(_ t: Ticks, _ grid: Ticks) -> Ticks {
293	        let q = t / grid
294	        return (t % grid != 0 && t < 0 ? q - 1 : q) * grid
295	    }
296	
297	    private static func up(_ t: Ticks, _ grid: Ticks) -> Ticks {
298	        let q = t / grid
299	        return (t % grid != 0 && t > 0 ? q + 1 : q) * grid
300	    }
301	
302	    /// A run's source span widened outward to the grid, bounded by its
303	    /// neighbours' grid points inward; nil when nothing is left.
304	    static func gridded(_ run: Run, grid: Ticks) -> SilenceDetector.Span? {
305	        guard grid > 0 else { return nil }
306	        let start = max(down(run.source.start, grid), up(run.previousEnd, grid))
307	        let end = min(up(run.source.end, grid), down(run.nextStart, grid))
308	        guard end > start else { return nil }
309	        return SilenceDetector.Span(start: start, end: end)
310	    }
311	
312	    /// A source span in project time, its start snapped up and its end down
313	    /// to the frame grid; nil when nothing is left.
314	    static func placed(
315	        _ source: SilenceDetector.Span, in job: Transcriber.Job, fps: Fps
316	    ) -> SilenceDetector.Span? {
317	        let span = SilenceDetector.Span(
318	            start: SilenceDetector.snapUpToFrame(
319	                MediaTranscript.project(source.start, in: job), fps: fps),
320	            end: SilenceDetector.snapDownToFrame(
321	                MediaTranscript.project(source.end, in: job), fps: fps))
322	        guard span.end > span.start else { return nil }
323	        return span
324	    }
325	
326	    // MARK: - Detection
327	
328	    /// The candidates, what was dropped and why, and the merged ranges.
329	    static func detect(_ input: Input) -> Outcome {
330	        // Every neighbour's non-filler words in project time, read once.
331	        let guarded: [(clip: UInt32, words: [CaptionCues.Word])] = input.neighbours.map {
332	            ($0.job.clip,
333	             MediaTranscript.words(for: $0.job, in: $0.file).filter {
334	                 !FillerWords.isFiller($0.text)
335	             })
336	        }
337	        var candidates: [Candidate] = []
338	        var dropped: [Dropped] = []
339	        for clip in input.clips {
340	            let id = clip.job.clip
341	            for run in runs(of: clip.file, in: clip.job) {
342	                guard let source = gridded(run, grid: grid),
343	                    let span = placed(source, in: clip.job, fps: input.fps)
344	                else {
345	                    dropped.append(Dropped(clip: id, words: run.words, reason: .tooShort))
346	                    continue
347	                }
348	                if let reason = conflict(span, clip: id, guarded: guarded, input: input) {
349	                    dropped.append(Dropped(clip: id, words: run.words, reason: reason))
350	                    continue
351	                }
352	                candidates.append(Candidate(clip: id, words: run.words, source: source, span: span))
353	            }
354	        }
355	        return Outcome(
356	            spans: SilenceDetector.merged(candidates.map(\.span)), candidates: candidates,
357	            dropped: dropped, scope: input.scope,
358	            clips: Set(input.clips.map { $0.job.clip }).sorted(),
359	            needsTranscript: input.needsTranscript, skipped: input.skipped, locked: input.locked)
360	    }
361	
362	    /// Why a span may not be cut, in TR-9's order: another clip's word, a
363	    /// nest clip, a transition wall; nil when it may.
364	    private static func conflict(
365	        _ span: SilenceDetector.Span, clip: UInt32,
366	        guarded: [(clip: UInt32, words: [CaptionCues.Word])], input: Input
367	    ) -> DropReason? {
368	        for neighbour in guarded where neighbour.clip != clip {
369	            if let word = neighbour.words.first(where: {
370	                SilenceDetector.overlap(span, SilenceDetector.Span(start: $0.start, end: $0.end)) > 0
371	            }) {
372	                return .overlapsWord(clip: neighbour.clip, text: word.text)
373	            }
374	        }
375	        if let nest = input.nests.first(where: { SilenceDetector.overlap(span, $0.span) > 0 }) {
376	            return .nest(clip: nest.clip)
377	        }
378	        if input.walls.contains(where: { SilenceDetector.overlap(span, $0) > 0 }) {
379	            return .transition
380	        }
381	        return nil
382	    }
383	}

3	/// The candidate-span wash Remove Silences puts on the timeline while its
4	/// sheet is up (road map 2 phase 3a) — the bodies of the two one-line hooks
5	/// `TimelineView.swift` carries, in the shape `TimelineView+Rename.swift` and
6	/// `EditorViewController+Edge.swift`'s `extension TimelineView` set.
7	///
8	/// **Why a hook and not an overlay view.** The other sanctioned route for an
9	/// extension that needs to draw is a subview found by kind, the way
10	/// `EditorViewController+Eyedropper.swift` finds its overlay on the canvas.
11	/// It cannot work here. `TimelineRulerView.draw` opens by filling its whole
12	/// bounds with `DS.chromeBackground`, so an overlay positioned BELOW the
13	/// ruler is painted straight over and one positioned above it hides the
14	/// ticks, the marker flags and the playhead's head. In the lanes it would be
15	/// wrong the other way: the in/out wash is drawn before the clip loop, i.e.
16	/// UNDER the clips, and a subview always paints over its superview's own
17	/// `draw`. Two one-line calls inside the frozen `draw`s are the only way to
18	/// land in the same two places the in/out range lands, which is what "in the
19	/// in/out style" means.
20	///
21	/// The ink is `DS.timelineCandidateShade` — the range's coral at roughly
22	/// double the wash — because a candidate span and an in/out range can overlap
23	/// and one constant would make them indistinguishable.

27	extension TimelineContentView {
28	    /// Called from `draw(_:)` immediately after the in/out wash and before the
29	    /// clip loop, so the shading sits UNDER the clips exactly as the range's
30	    /// does. Both views draw in content coordinates, so a span's x comes
31	    /// straight from the layout with no scroll offset of its own.
32	    func drawCandidateSpans(owner: TimelineView, layout: TimelineLayout) {
33	        let spans = owner.candidateSpans
34	        guard !spans.isEmpty, layout.trackCount > 0 else { return }
35	        DS.timelineCandidateShade.setFill()
36	        for span in spans where span.end > span.start {
37	            NSRect(
38	                x: layout.x(for: span.start), y: layout.lanesTop,
39	                width: layout.width(of: span.end - span.start),
40	                height: layout.lanesHeight
41	            ).fill()
42	        }
43	    }
44	}

49	    /// Called from `draw(_:)` after the band's own opaque fill and its in/out
50	    /// wash, and before the ticks — the same slot, for the same reason: the

53	        let spans = owner.candidateSpans

3	/// The agent's silence tool: the read half of Remove Silences.
4	///
5	/// `detect_silence` is an APP-STATE tool, not an op — it changes nothing and
6	/// registers no undo step. It exists because the detection is Swift's (the
7	/// waveform peaks the package caches are not in the model, and the core does
8	/// no sample work at all — spec §7), so an agent that could only call
9	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` would have to invent the ranges from nothing. The
10	/// pair is deliberate and mirrors the sheet exactly: `detect_silence` is what
11	/// `SilenceSheetController` shows in its live readout, and
12	/// `ripple_delete_ranges` is what its Remove button sends.
13	///
14	/// It stays on the MAIN thread, and so out of `AgentServer.offMainTools`,
15	/// because that set's criterion is "waits for something the main thread has
16	/// to deliver or must not be doing", not "touches the disk":
17	/// `consolidate_media` copies whole media libraries on main and says why, and
18	/// `import_captions` parses a file on main for the same reason. Reading a few
19	/// hundred KB of `cache/peaks/<id>.bin` and making one arithmetic pass over
20	/// it waits on nothing and has no completion to deliver, and being off main
21	/// would cost an `onMain` hop for every document touch — which is where the
22	/// real bugs in this file's neighbours have been.
23	extension AgentServer {
24	
25	    /// The longest a duration argument may be, `snappedTick`'s own ±9.0e15:
26	    /// past it `refine`'s `run.start + padding` overflows. Finding 1 above.
27	    /// Not private: `AgentCatalog+Audio` PUBLISHES it as both durations'
28	    /// `maximum`, so the bound a caller reads and the bound the handler
29	    /// enforces are one number (the second sceptic pass, road map 4 §8).
30	    static let durationCeiling = 9_000_000_000_000_000
31	
32	    /// `detect_silence` — Clip ▸ Remove Silences…
33	    /// (`SilenceSheetController`, whose four controls are these four
34	    /// arguments and whose live "N cuts · removes M:SS" line is this
35	    /// result). Nothing is edited: feed `ranges` to `ripple_delete_ranges`
36	    /// to make the cut, which is what that sheet's button does. The
37	    /// `protected_nests` note is the tool's spelling of the sheet's nest note.
38	    ///
39	    /// Quiet is measured IN THE MIX — the peak bucket times the plan's audio
40	    /// envelope at that tick — so a clip turned down, faded, ducked, muted or
41	    /// silenced by another track's solo is quiet here exactly as it is in the
42	    /// speakers. A tick no clip in scope covers is not a candidate at all: a
43	    /// hole in the timeline is not dead air to be removed.
44	    func detectSilence(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
45	        let document = try target(a)
46	        let clips = try optionalClipsArg(a, "clips", document)
47	        // `clips` is the sheet's scope popup, spelled as the thing an agent
48	        // actually has: ids. Naming any runs the popup's "Selected clips"
49	        // over exactly those — `read` takes a selection override for this
50	        // very reason — and omitting the key takes the sheet's own opening
51	        // rule, which is the document's selection when it holds anything
52	        // with sound and everything audible otherwise. The result reports
53	        // which of the two answered, because "nothing was found" and
54	        // "nothing was looked at" are different answers and no caller can
55	        // tell them apart from an empty list.
56	        guard let input = SilenceDetector.read(from: document, selection: clips.map { Set($0) })
57	        else {
58	            throw ToolError(
59	                message: "The project's audio plan could not be read, so there is nothing to "
60	                    + "measure silence against.")
61	        }
62	        let (settings, modeNote) = try silenceSettings(
63	            a, scope: clips == nil ? input.defaultScope : .selected,
64	            voiceAvailable: input.voiceAvailable)
65	        let outcome = SilenceDetector.detect(input, settings: settings)
66	
67	        var result: [String: Any] = [
68	            "ok": true,
69	            "ranges": outcome.spans.map { [$0.start, $0.end] },
70	            "count": outcome.spans.count,
71	            "removes": outcome.removed,
72	            "scope": outcome.scope.rawValue,
73	            "clips": outcome.clips.map { Int($0) },
74	            "threshold_db": settings.thresholdDB,
75	            "min_length": settings.minLength,
76	            "padding": settings.padding,

96	        }

98	        // the level test and the voice test are each still waiting on — so a
99	        // caller that only ever read that key still knows to call again.
100	        let pendingPeaks = Set(outcome.pendingMedia)
101	        let pendingUnion = outcome.mode == .voice
102	            ? pendingPeaks.union(outcome.voicePending) : pendingPeaks

104	            result["pending_peaks"] = pendingUnion.sorted().map { Int($0) }
105	            // "Nothing inside them is proposed for removal" is a PROMISE about
106	            // the ranges in this same reply, so it is made only about the
107	            // media it holds for. A media with no peaks is never quiet in
108	            // LEVEL mode, so there it holds for every waiter; in VOICE mode a
109	            // media whose waveform is missing but whose speech has landed is
110	            // judged by the model and spans inside it ARE proposed — and the
111	            // sentence used to deny exactly the ranges it was printed beside
112	            // (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R3·1).
113	            let waiter = outcome.mode == .voice ? Set(outcome.voicePending) : pendingPeaks

115	            // the mode: the gain FLOOR is asked before either cache
116	            // (`SilenceDetector.isQuiet`), so a clip the mix has turned down,
117	            // faded, ducked or muted is quiet with nothing on disk at all and
118	            // its spans are right here (the reader review, road map 4 §8,
119	            // finding 2). Whatever the answer proposes inside is dropped from
120	            // the promise, and the clips it is proposed inside are named in
121	            // their own clause (#107).
122	            let proposedInside = waiter.intersection(outcome.proposedMedia)
123	            let blocked = waiter.subtracting(proposedInside)
124	            let waveformOnly = pendingUnion.subtracting(waiter)
125	            var waiting =
126	                "Analysis is still running for \(pendingUnion.count) media file(s); call "
127	                + "again in a moment."
128	            if !blocked.isEmpty {
129	                waiting += blocked.count == pendingUnion.count
130	                    ? " Nothing inside them is proposed for removal."
131	                    : " Nothing inside \(blocked.count) of them is proposed for removal."
132	            }
133	            let mixInside = Self.clipIDs(outcome.mixAnswers(inside: waiter))
134	            if mixInside.count == 1 {
135	                waiting +=
136	                    " Clip \(mixInside[0]) holds spans that ARE proposed here: the mix turns "
137	                    + "it down far enough to be quiet before either cache is asked."
138	            } else if mixInside.count > 1 {
139	                waiting +=
140	                    " Clips \(Self.listed(mixInside)) hold spans that ARE proposed here: the "
141	                    + "mix turns them down far enough to be quiet before either cache is asked."
142	            }
143	            if !waveformOnly.isEmpty {
144	                // The mirror image of the promise above, and it needs the
145	                // same intersection (the reader review's second sceptic pass,
146	                // road map 4 §8). "Spans inside them ARE proposed here" is a
147	                // claim about ranges in this very reply, so a waveform waiter
148	                // the answer proposes NOTHING inside — every clip of it holds
149	                // no voice, so the missing waveform blocks the lot — must not
150	                // be told it has them.
151	                let proposedHere = waveformOnly.intersection(outcome.proposedMedia)
152	                let silentHere = waveformOnly.subtracting(proposedHere)
153	                let ending: String
154	                if silentHere.isEmpty {

156	                } else if proposedHere.isEmpty {
157	                    ending = ", and nothing inside them is proposed here."
158	                } else {

162	                }

165	                    + "WAVEFORM that has not landed, which in voice mode decides only a clip "
166	                    + "holding no voice" + ending

168	                // model's, name the clip (#107): a clip that holds no voice
169	                // is proposed without its waveform only because the mix
170	                // already turned it down, and another clip of the same file
171	                // the mix left alone is not. No `voicePending` arm is needed
172	                // here — a voice waiter is in `waiter` above and never in
173	                // `waveformOnly`.
174	                let mixOnly = Self.clipIDs(outcome.mixAnswers(inside: waveformOnly))
175	                if mixOnly.count == 1 {
176	                    waiting +=
177	                        " Clip \(mixOnly[0]) is proposed only where the mix already turns it "
178	                        + "down far enough to be quiet."
179	                } else if mixOnly.count > 1 {
180	                    waiting +=
181	                        " Clips \(Self.listed(mixOnly)) are proposed only where the mix "

191	        if byLevel.count == 1 {
192	            notes.append("Clip \(byLevel[0]) holds no voice and was judged by level.")

194	            notes.append(

196	        }

198	        // held back at a nest's wall, dropped without a word, reads as "there
199	        // is no dead air here". A listed nest clip is one a quiet run of the
200	        // SCOPED voices crossed (`SilenceDetector+Walls.swift`'s
201	        // `excludingNests`); the nest's own sound is not tested, so it MAY
202	        // hold dead air, and the reader is told to look, not that it does.

226	    /// "that file" / "them" / "2 of them", so a clause about SOME of the
227	    /// waiters never says "the rest" of a sentence that was not printed
228	    /// (the reader review, road map 4 §8, finding 4).
229	    private static func subject(_ count: Int, of total: Int) -> String {
230	        count == total ? (count == 1 ? "that file" : "them") : "\(count) of them"
231	    }
232	
233	    /// The distinct clip ids of some voices' answers, ascending — the tool
234	    /// names a clip by id, as `Transcriber+Jobs` tags one (#107).
235	    private static func clipIDs(_ answers: [SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer]) -> [UInt32] {
236	        Set(answers.map { $0.clip }).sorted()
237	    }
238	
239	    /// "3, 7, 9".
240	    private static func listed(_ ids: [UInt32]) -> String {
241	        ids.map { String($0) }.joined(separator: ", ")
242	    }
243	
244	    /// The three numbers, read in the sheet's own units and refused by name.
245	    ///
246	    /// The sheet clamps its controls to `Settings`' published ranges because
247	    /// a slider must land somewhere; a tool does not, and clamping an
248	    /// argument silently would report a detection the caller did not ask
249	    /// for. What is refused here is what is not a level or not a length at
250	    /// all — everything else is passed through and named back in the result,
251	    /// so a caller reading `threshold_db` sees what actually ran.
252	    private func silenceSettings(
253	        _ a: [String: Any], scope: SilenceDetector.Scope, voiceAvailable: Bool
254	    ) throws -> (SilenceDetector.Settings, String?) {
255	        var settings = SilenceDetector.Settings(scope: scope)
256	        var note: String?
257	        if let modeString = try stringArg(a, "mode") {
258	            guard let mode = SilenceDetector.Mode(rawValue: modeString) else {
259	                throw ToolError(
260	                    message: "mode must be \"voice\" or \"level\".")
261	            }
262	            if mode == .voice, !voiceAvailable {
263	                throw ToolError(
264	                    message: "The voice model could not be used; call with mode: \"level\".")
265	            }
266	            settings.mode = mode
267	        } else if !voiceAvailable {
268	            settings.mode = .level
269	            note = "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level."
270	        }
271	        if let voiceConfidence = try doubleArg(a, "voice_confidence") {
272	            guard settings.mode == .voice else {
273	                throw ToolError(
274	                    message: "voice_confidence only applies in mode: \"voice\".")
275	            }
276	            guard voiceConfidence.isFinite,
277	                SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.contains(voiceConfidence)
278	            else {
279	                throw ToolError(
280	                    message: "voice_confidence must be a number in "
281	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.lowerBound)…"
282	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.upperBound).")
283	            }
284	            settings.voiceConfidence = voiceConfidence
285	        }
286	        if let thresholdDB = try doubleArg(a, "threshold_db") {
287	            // Above full scale every bucket of every recording counts as
288	            // quiet and the whole timeline comes back as one candidate.
289	            // Peaks are unclamped and a hot source really does read over
290	            // 1.0, so this is a caller's mistake — a level in gain, or a
291	            // sign forgotten — rather than an impossible number.
292	            guard thresholdDB.isFinite, thresholdDB <= 0 else {
293	                throw ToolError(
294	                    message: "threshold_db must be a level at or below 0 dBFS (full scale); "
295	                        + "the default is \(SilenceDetector.Settings.defaultThresholdDB).")
296	            }
297	            settings.thresholdDB = thresholdDB
298	        }
299	        // Both lengths are DURATIONS, and a duration is not a position: they
300	        // are read as given, by the whole-number reader, and are NOT snapped
301	        // to the frame grid. The sheet's own two fields are not snapped
302	        // either (`SilenceSheetController.silenceSettings`'
303	        // `ReelTime.ticks(seconds:)`) and this tool exists to mirror it; the
304	        // frame rule stays where it belongs, on the span BOUNDS `refine`
305	        // produces, so no sub-frame time reaches an op from here. Going
306	        // through `optionalTimeArg` cost that mirror at the DEFAULT rate:
307	        // at 30 fps it ran `padding: 30000` — the sheet's own 0.05 s — as
308	        // 40000, ran `min_length: 45000` as 40000, and dropped
309	        // `padding: 9999` to 0, cutting the material the caller asked to
310	        // keep (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R1·1).
311	        //
312	        // What `optionalTimeArg` DID carry and a duration still needs is its
313	        // CEILING: `refine` adds the padding to a run's start, and a padding
314	        // at `Int64.max` overflowed and killed the app rather than answering
315	        // (the reader review, road map 4 §8, finding 1). The bound is
316	        // `snappedTick`'s own ±9.0e15, refused in a sentence naming the
317	        // argument. The sheet's two fields cannot reach it — they clamp to
318	        // `minLengthRange` and `paddingRange` — so the guard belongs here,
319	        // on the one caller that is not a slider.
320	        if let minLength = try intArg(a, "min_length") {
321	            guard minLength >= 0, minLength <= Self.durationCeiling else {
322	                throw ToolError(
323	                    message: "min_length must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
324	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
325	            }
326	            settings.minLength = Ticks(minLength)
327	        }
328	        if let padding = try intArg(a, "padding") {
329	            guard padding >= 0, padding <= Self.durationCeiling else {
330	                throw ToolError(
331	                    message: "padding must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
332	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
333	            }
334	            settings.padding = Ticks(padding)
335	        }
336	        return (settings, note)
337	    }

content.content:
- **The service can miss a filler.** A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut. A filler it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in captions.
- **Protection needs a transcript.** A filler cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a transcript. Speech on another unlocked track with no transcript isn't protected.
- **Up to a frame can remain.** Inward frame snapping can leave a frame of room tone, or of a filler, behind.
- **Wait for analysis.** After import, Remove Silences proposes nothing inside a file until its analysis is ready: the waveform in Level mode, the voice analysis in Voice mode (and the waveform too for a clip with no voice), except where the mix already makes it quiet.
- **Voice mode can miss a soft first word** in a quiet recording; raise **Keep at ends:** if a word is clipped.
- **Singing and voice-like instruments** may read as speech.
- **A clip that holds any voice is judged by voice for its whole length**, so a long music clip with a little speech in it isn't judged by level. Limit the scope (**In:** Selected clips) to keep music out.
- **A voice panned hard to one side** sounds quieter to the voice model.
- **In a reversed clip** a cut edge can be off by up to 32 ms.
- **Nests and transitions block cuts.** Quiet or fillers inside a nest, or in a transition's overlap, are never cut from outside the nest. Open the nest first.

See also: [Editing](editing.md) for ripple delete and Close Gap, [Audio](audio.md) for volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, which all affect what Remove Silences hears, and [MCP](mcp.md) for the full tool reference.

60:## How a ripple closes holes
65:- A clip moves if it starts at or after the end of the hole. When you ripple-delete clips, a clip on another track that spans the hole stays where it is, and isn't shortened.
68:- A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. A ripple is never stopped by the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
70:One thing does stop a ripple. If it would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline, as a sound leading its picture in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) can, nothing moves, and the foot of the inspector names both clips.
74:An agent can cut a list of time ranges out of the timeline as one edit and one undo step, with `ripple_delete_ranges`. It shows as Ripple Delete under **Edit ▸ Undo**. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) make the same cut from their sheets.
76:Ranges that touch or overlap merge into one before anything is cut, so two ranges that meet leave one hole, and all the cuts use times from the timeline as it was before the edit. Each range then behaves as [a ripple-deleted range](#ripple-delete-a-range) does: locked tracks are left alone and markers don't move. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/).

fixed.was: Markers stay at their times "as they do under every ripple".
fixed.now: "as they do under every ripple delete". An insert and a retime are ripples too, and they do move markers.
fixed.evidence: core/src/edit_time.rs:290-298 (ripple family leaves markers), core/src/edit.rs:138-139 (insert_time and retime_range move markers), core/src/edit_time.rs:455

fixed.was: "a cut can leave up to a frame of room tone, or of a filler, behind", which reads as one frame in total.
fixed.now: "each edge of a cut can leave up to a frame…". Both edges snap inward on their own.

fixed.was: "A nest's sound still counts.", stated for both commands and every scope.
fixed.now: "In Remove Silences a nest's sound still counts when In: is All audible clips." Filler removal doesn't read nests. Under Selected clips, a nest's inner segments carry inner clip ids, so they aren't in scope.

fixed.was: "In a reversed clip, a Remove Silences cut edge can be off by up to 32 ms."
fixed.now: "Remove Silences measures a reversed clip as it plays." The Remove Filler Words sentence stays.
fixed.evidence: app/Sources/MediaPeaks.swift:101-118 (window mirrored about the pivot), app/Sources/ReverseMirror.swift:41-48 (the only reversed-specific error is one extra bucket at an exactly aligned window end; no 32 ms bound follows from it), app/Sources/Transcriber+Jobs.swift:112

fixed.was: Judge by default: "Voice".
fixed.now: "Voice, or Level if the voice model can't be used".

fixed.was: "a clip the mix turns down below it is quiet"
fixed.now: "a clip the mix turns down to it or lower is quiet". The test is gain at or under the limit.

fixed.was: Selected clips greyed out when nothing selected makes a sound, with muted clips as the only exception named.
fixed.now: Adds "as does a selected nest". A nest clip's id is never a plan segment's clip, so a selected nest answers All audible clips and the row is disabled.

fixed.was: "so a frame more of room tone can remain"
fixed.now: "so up to a frame more of room tone can remain at each end"

fixed.was: "An open sheet drops the old answers at once", as if a person could relink under the sheet.
fixed.now: "If an agent relinks one while the sheet is open, the sheet drops the old answers at once…". Every editor action is off under a sheet, so only the relink_media tool can reach it.

removed: how-cleanup-cuts-work, Good to know: the 32 ms bound on a Remove Silences cut edge in a reversed clip. The code doesn't settle that number. The only reversed-specific error it records is one extra bucket at an exactly aligned window end (ReverseMirror.swift:41-48).
guide_errors: docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:178: "In a reversed clip a cut edge can be off by up to 32 ms." The code doesn't support this figure. The mirror's only recorded cost is one extra bucket at an exactly aligned window end, and a 32 ms chunk grid applies to every clip in Voice mode, not only reversed ones.
docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md:172: "Up to a frame can remain." This is per edge, so up to a frame at each end of a cut.

Guide wording "a nest's sound still counts" (source of the cleanup-nests-protected feature row): true only for Remove Silences with All audible clips. Under Selected clips a nest's inner segments are out of scope, and a selected nest alone counts as nothing audible, so Selected clips is greyed out.
Guide wording "Markers do not move… as under every ripple" (source of the cleanup-markers-stay feature row): insert_time and retime_range move markers, so it should say every ripple delete.
Guide wording on relinking (source of the cleanup-silence-relink feature row): only an agent's relink_media can reach an open sheet. A person's Relink… is blocked while the sheet is up.

Not settled by code alone: the formatter's out-of-range rejection is AppKit behaviour, and I did not see it run. The page's beep on Remove rests on endSheetFieldEditing (app/Sources/Sheets.swift:227-233) and the formatter bounds (SilenceSheetController.swift:186-194). Shading clearing when the window closes rests on the teardown in viewDidDisappear. I checked everything by reading the code and did not drive the app.
